summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of mitochondrial myopathy, coronary artery disease, and hypogammaglobulinemia was admitted for a scheduled IVIG infusion using Privigen, a low osmolar agent, due to prior adverse reactions with other formulations. During the infusion, he developed hypertension with systolic pressure up to 200 and transient chest tightness, which was distinct from his usual anginal symptoms and not associated with EKG changes. He also experienced dizziness and a delayed episode of chest tightness and shortness of breath, which resolved without intervention. His blood pressure was managed by slowing the infusion rate, and no medication changes were made. His mitochondrial myopathy and cardiac conditions remained stable. Mild acidosis and dehydration improved with supportive care. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up on blood pressure and discuss infusion tolerance with his allergist.
